notices.summary_row: Residential lien: written contract and licensure statement in the contract
notices.hold_reason: no prescribed wording; the statute only lists required content

notices.cite: MCL 445.113 (statement and notice of cancellation); 445.112 (right to cancel)
notices.format: Statement in immediate proximity to the buyer's signature; notice of cancellation in duplicate, attached or printed on the reverse; not less than 10-point bold and 2 points larger than the contract text
notices.support: Michigan does have a fixed statement and a fixed duplicate notice. The statement has three sentences, the third unique to Michigan (courier pick-up). Type rule: "not less than 10-point bold type and shall be 2 points larger than the text of the contract".
notices.summary_row: Buyer statement near signature (three sentences, incl. courier sentence) and duplicate notice of cancellation
notices.hold_reason: The block is the whole of MCL 445.113 with subsections 4 to 6 (exceptions for telephone and utility sales) around the notices, and the official PDF prints the literal characters " for the notice's quotation marks.

changes.support: Unlike the federal rule and most states, Saturday does not count in Michigan.
A written agreement or offer to purchase and the notice of cancellation attached to the agreement or offer shall be written in the same language as that used in any oral presentation

changes.new: Business day is Monday through Friday; Saturday, Sunday and ten named holidays do not count (445.111(c)).
changes.support: "Business day" (445.111(c)) "means Monday through Friday and does not include Saturday, Sunday, or" ten named holidays.

unsure: MI-lien: the 570.1114 statement lists required content and also names electricians, plumbers and mechanical contractors, so it is not clear a general contractor's contract needs every part; no sentence is prescribed so nothing is loaded.
MI-cancel: 445.113 applies only to a home solicitation sale of more than $25 solicited at the buyer's residence; the builder only knows 'sold at the customer's home', so the trigger is approximate.
